claims.text: HVOF spraying produces a refined microstructure in FCC/BCC HEA coatings.
HVOF spraying enhances compressive residual stresses in FCC/BCC HEA coatings.
Refined grain boundaries inhibit dislocation mobility.
Compressive residual-stress fields inhibit dislocation mobility.
Reduced dislocation mobility delays progressive plastic deformation and improves creep resistance under sustained loading.
High-velocity spraying generates a non-equilibrium microstructure in the HEA coating.
Conventionally deposited HEA coatings have coarser grain structures than HVOF-sprayed coatings.
Conventionally deposited HEA coatings have lower or minimal compressive residual stress compared with HVOF-sprayed coatings.
Sustained stress under continuous loading drives creep deformation.
Under identical loading and temperature conditions, HVOF-sprayed coatings will have a lower creep strain rate than conventionally deposited coatings.
Under identical loading and temperature conditions, HVOF-sprayed coatings will show a later onset of detectable plastic deformation than conventionally deposited coatings.
The proposed creep-resistance improvement applies within service-relevant stress and temperature ranges but may fail at extreme temperatures or loads beyond design limits.
Variation in HVOF process parameters and interactions among phase constituents affect the magnitude of creep-resistance improvement.
